## Strongest exact statement

The protected predecessor claim is deterministically replay-closed at exactly its stated conditional scope. Using only the protected packet, and treating the 333444 state description as a hypothesis rather than as an independently established upstream fact, the following implications replay without contradiction: the no-(r-1)-consecutive-D1 fan bound gives d1(v) <= 2r-3; the clean-line parity argument forces at least one bounded transverse elementary piece of triangle-use zero; ordinary-endpoint capacities and D1/D2 blocking give n-h <= 2U+D1-B; saturation of the 333444 local caps forces exactly two admissible triple-core ray words and eight admissible quadruple-core ray words with every D2 ray isolated; every simple cubic graph on six labeled vertices is either a triangular prism or K3,3, with labeled counts 60 and 10 respectively; K3,3 cannot be the straight-line elementary D2 core graph; and every saturated prism produces an arrangement vertex in the relative interior of a D2 edge, contradiction.

This validates the predecessor's conditional replay claim only. ## Derivation

For the fan bound, suppose an r-fold core has r-1 consecutive D1 rays. The stated D1 incidence property forces r consecutive triangular sectors bounded by r+1 successive radial rays. Let their far endpoints be P0,...,Pr and their opposite supports A0,...,A(r-1). At each internal Pi, the D1 radial segment has an ordinary far endpoint. The two adjacent opposite supports through Pi are both nonradial, so ordinariness forces them to be the same line. Hence all Aj coincide. The boundary rays P0 and Pr are r ray-steps apart among 2r radial rays, so they are antipodal halves of one support through the core. The common opposite support contains both P0 and Pr and therefore is that radial support, making the end triangles degenerate. Thus no cyclic block of r-1 rays can all be D1. Counting length-(r-1) cyclic blocks gives (r-1)d1(v) <= 2r(r-2), whose integer consequence for r>=3 is d1(v) <= 2r-3.

For clean-line parity, let the clean line have m=n-1 ordinary crossings, with m odd. Let xi and yi record triangular incidence on the two sides of the bounded clean-line segment between crossings i and i+1, and set x0=y0=xm=ym=0. The two-ordinary-endpoint geometry gives xi+yi<=1. The two elementary pieces of the ith transverse line adjacent to the clean line have triangle-use counts x(i-1)+xi and y(i-1)+yi. Assume for contradiction that every bounded transverse piece has use exactly one. A positive-use piece is bounded, so use two is impossible; conversely, under the assumption, a zero-use piece is unbounded. At the first crossing at least one transverse direction is bounded. Reflection permits x1=1,y1=0. Induction then gives x_i=0 for every even i and y_i=0 for every odd i. The induction step is deterministic: if the preceding same-side indicator is one, the next must be zero to avoid use two; if it is zero, the already-established opposite invariant makes the adjacent piece use zero and hence unbounded, forcing the next transverse intersection to the opposite half-plane and therefore forcing the opposite piece at the next crossing to be bounded. Since m-1 is even, x(m-1)=0. If y(m-1)=0, both pieces at the last transverse line have use zero although at least one must be bounded. If y(m-1)=1, the lower piece at the first transverse line and upper piece at the last both have use zero and therefore are unbounded, but those two nonparallel lines intersect in one half-plane, making one of those two pieces bounded. Both cases contradict the assumption.

For endpoint capacity, a clean-line charge can enter a fixed target elementary segment only through an ordinary endpoint, and an ordinary endpoint has exactly one nonradial arrangement line available. Therefore a target with two ordinary endpoints has capacity at most two, a target with one ordinary endpoint has capacity at most one, and a target with no ordinary endpoint has capacity zero. If a D1 ray borders a D2 ray at a multiple core, their common triangular sector has an opposite support through the ordinary far endpoint of the D1 segment and the multiple far endpoint of the D2 segment. That support is the unique nonradial line through the ordinary endpoint and is not clean because it contains a multiple point. Thus that D1 target cannot receive a clean-line charge. Counting each blocked D1 ray once yields n-h <= 2U+D1-B.

In the conditional 333444 state, the fan caps are 3 at each triple core and 5 at each quadruple core. Their total is 24, equal to the stated D1 total, so every core saturates. A triple core therefore has three D1 and three D2 rays with no two consecutive D1 rays, forcing alternation. A quadruple core has five D1 and three D2 rays; the three D1 gaps between D2 rays have sizes at most two and total five, so their multiset is {2,2,1}. Hence every gap is nonempty and every D2 ray is isolated.

For the six-core graph, the complement of a simple cubic graph on six vertices is simple 2-regular. Its connected components are cycles of length at least three, so the only possible cycle partitions of six are 6 and 3+3. Complementing gives respectively the triangular prism and K3,3. The labeled C6 count is 6!/12=60, and the labeled two-triangle count is binomial(6,3)/2=10. Because D2 edges are elementary straight arrangement segments, two such edges cannot cross in their interiors without producing an arrangement vertex inside both, so the D2 core graph is planar. K3,3 is excluded by the elementary planar bipartite bound E<=2V-4, since 9>8.

A prism contains a D2 3-cycle. Its three core vertices cannot be collinear, because then the elementary edge joining the extreme pair would contain the third core. At any corner A of the resulting geometric triangle, the two incident D2 rays are nonadjacent in the cyclic order because all D2 rays are isolated. Therefore the open angular interval equal to the triangle's interior angle contains another arrangement ray. Any ray strictly inside angle BAC has direction alpha(B-A)+beta(C-A) with alpha,beta>0 and its support meets BC at (alpha B+beta C)/(alpha+beta), strictly inside segment BC. That intersection is an arrangement vertex in the relative interior of the D2 edge BC, contradicting elementaryness. Hence the saturated prism state is impossible.

## Verification / falsification hooks

I independently exhaustively enumerated the finite objects described in the protected packet rather than trusting the predecessor's reported output.

For triple cores, all 2^6=64 binary cyclic ray words were scanned at weight three, rejecting any word containing a cyclic run of r-1=2 D1 rays. Exactly two survive: 010101 and 101010. Both have every D2 ray isolated.

For quadruple cores, all 2^8=256 binary cyclic ray words were scanned at weight five, rejecting any word containing a cyclic run of r-1=3 D1 rays. Exactly eight survive: 01011011, 01101011, 01101101, 10101101, 10110101, 10110110, 11010110, and 11011010. Every survivor has every D2 ray isolated.

For the graph classification, I performed an independent scan of all 2^15=32768 labeled simple graphs on six vertices and selected those whose degree sequence is (2,2,2,2,2,2), i.e. complements of labeled cubic graphs. Exactly 70 survive. Their connected-component-size partitions are exactly 60 instances of (6) and 10 instances of (3,3), reproducing the prism/K3,3 split without using the predecessor's nine-edge enumerator. A separate direct cubic scan also returned 70 graphs, with 60 having two triangles and 10 having none.

The non-finite proof steps have explicit local falsification points. The fan proof would fail only if an ordinary endpoint admitted two distinct nonradial arrangement supports or if r ray-steps did not identify antipodal rays. The clean-line proof would fail only if a zero-use elementary transverse piece could be bounded under the contradiction hypothesis, or if two adjacent transverse supports could avoid intersecting in the opposite half-plane after one adjacent piece is unbounded. The prism obstruction would fail only if a ray strictly inside a nondegenerate triangle angle could avoid the relative interior of the opposite side. None of those failures is compatible with the stated affine-line and elementary-segment hypotheses.
